title: Check Point management server intrusions (GT13), Nov 2026

subject.name: Check Point
subject.about: Check Point Software Technologies is a cyber security company, founded in 1993, that makes firewalls and other security products used by businesses and governments to protect their networks.

disclaimer: Made for entertainment using AI. Not endorsed by Check Point, GreyNoise, CISA, any news outlet, company, government agency, or anyone else named.
size_basis: GreyNoise counts 24 servers at 22 organisations in 17 countries, including government, energy and finance. The servers control company firewalls, so the reach inside each victim could be wide. No victim has been named.
who_is_affected: Organisations that run Check Point Security Management servers, mainly ones reachable from the internet. GreyNoise counts 22 victims in 17 countries. Ordinary consumers are not directly affected. Check Point customers should install the July 2026 fix and limit who can log in to management servers.

known.text: Check Point confirmed in July 2026 that attackers exploited a login-bypass flaw in its management servers (CVE-2026-16232), and CISA lists it as exploited.
Check Point released a fix for that flaw on July 22, 2026.
Check Point says a separate wave from Oct 30 compromised a couple of dozen unpatched Check Point firewalls through a PHP flaw.

not_known.text: Whether Check Point, a victim or a government confirms GreyNoise's count of 22 organisations hit.
How the attacker first got into the Check Point servers. The root cause is not published.
Whether the attacks are still going on after Nov 2.
